description: A DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL database cluster with a single node, with one database and one non-admin user for your app, reached over TLS with a password. Pick this when you need a Postgres database without running a server yourself. Access is restricted: only the user's own droplets named in allowed_droplet_request_ids and the IPv4 addresses in allowed_ip_addresses can connect, at least one of the two is needed, and the database is unreachable from anywhere else.
costHint: About $15 to $30 a month, depending on size.

variables.name: name
variables.label: Name
variables.description: Cluster name: 3 to 34 characters, starts with a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, not ending in a hyphen. A short suffix from the request is added to it.

variables.name: region
variables.label: Region
variables.description: Datacenter: nyc3 (New York), sfo3 (San Francisco), ams3 (Amsterdam), lon1 (London), fra1 (Frankfurt) or sgp1 (Singapore).

variables.name: size
variables.label: Size
variables.description: db-s-1vcpu-1gb (1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 10 GiB storage, about $15/month) or db-s-1vcpu-2gb (1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 30 GiB storage, about $30/month). Always a single node, so not highly available.

variables.name: database_name
variables.label: Database
variables.description: The database to create for the app (default app). Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters; not defaultdb, postgres, template0 or template1.

variables.name: user_name
variables.label: User
variables.description: The non-admin database user to create for the app (default app_user); DigitalOcean generates its password. Lowercase letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter, at most 63 characters; not doadmin or postgres, and not starting with pg_.

variables.name: allowed_droplet_request_ids
variables.label: Allowed droplets
variables.description: The request IDs of the user's own droplets that may connect, up to 10, taken from list_my_resources (a lowercase GUID such as 3f2b8c1e-5d4a-4e6f-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b). Only droplets the user requested and that are provisioned are accepted. Never use a droplet name, a DigitalOcean droplet ID or a tag. Give at least one droplet here or one address in allowed_ip_addresses: with neither, the request fails. An app on a droplet must have that droplet listed here to reach the database.

variables.name: allowed_ip_addresses
variables.label: Allowed IP addresses
variables.description: IPv4 addresses that may connect, up to 10, as CIDRs from /8 to /32: suggest the user's own IP as x.x.x.x/32. IPv6 isn't supported by DigitalOcean here, and 0.0.0.0/0 (anywhere) is refused. Give at least one address here or one droplet in allowed_droplet_request_ids: with neither, the request fails.

items.description: An IPv4 CIDR from /8 to /32, such as 203.0.113.7/32.

variables.name: project_request_id
variables.label: Project
variables.description: Optional: the request ID of one of the user's projects to put this in. Without one, it goes in the account's default project.

outputs.name: host
outputs.description: Public hostname to connect to, reachable only from the allowed droplets and IP addresses.

outputs.name: port
outputs.description: Port to connect to. Connections must use TLS (sslmode=require).

outputs.name: uri
outputs.description: Connection URI for the app's user and database, including the password.

outputs.name: admin_password
outputs.description: Password for the cluster's admin user, doadmin.

outputs.name: admin_uri
outputs.description: Connection URI for doadmin on defaultdb, including the password; for admin tasks such as granting the app's user CREATE on a schema.
